description: Post type codes observed: 1 = question (42,912 rows), 2 = answer (47,755 rows), 3 = 6, 4 = 639, 5 = 640, 6 = 9, 7 = 5. Codes other than 1 and 2 are site-specific post kinds and must not be treated as questions or answers.
scope: Interpreting the post type code on post rows

description: Titles and tags are populated only for question posts (post type 1); answer rows have null title and null tags. A title or tag condition therefore implicitly restricts the population to questions.
scope: Any condition or projection on post titles or tags

description: Stored title text preserves the case of the latest revision and can differ from the case used in a question: the post whose question wording is 'Computer Game Datasets' is stored as 'Computer game datasets', so an exact-case comparison returns no row. Earlier title wording survives only in post revision text.
scope: Matching a quoted title against stored title text

description: Display names are not unique: 40,325 accounts share 35,644 distinct names, and 1,563 names belong to more than one account (6,244 rows). The user identifier is the reliable key; a name lookup may return several accounts.
Only 3,425 of 38,930 vote records carry an acting user identifier (509 distinct users); the remainder are anonymous. Vote-based attribution to users is mostly unavailable.
Age is recorded for only 8,318 of 40,325 users (about 21%), and only 87 users exceed 65. Age filters silently exclude accounts with no recorded age.

Vote type codes observed: 2 = up vote (33,323), 5 = favorite (3,365), 1 = accepted by originator (1,451), 3 = down vote (444), 16 = 111, 15 = 72, 8 = bounty start (60), 9 = bounty close (59), 11 = undeletion (44), 10 = deletion (1). Codes 15 and 16 are not identified from the data.

A bounty amount is populated only on bounty start (type 8) and bounty close (type 9) vote records; observed values run from 50 to 200 for starts and 0 to 150 for closes. Bounty analysis must restrict to those vote types.

A post is closed when its closed-date field is non-null and never closed when that field is null. 1,610 of 91,966 posts carry a closed date. 'Not well-finished' means the closed date is null; 'well-finished' means it is present.
scope: Determining whether a post was closed or finished

description: Post tags are stored as angle-bracket-delimited tokens in one text field, for example <bayesian><prior><elicitation>. A tag must be matched as a whole token such as <r>; a plain substring comparison for 'r' also matches unrelated tags. The tag catalogue separately records each tag name and its usage count.
An elder user is a user whose recorded age is strictly greater than 65. Users without a recorded age are not elder users.
Referential checks found 36 comment rows and 41 revision rows whose post identifier has no matching post row; these are orphaned records left by deleted posts and disappear under inner joins.
scope: Joining comments or revisions to posts

description: Reputation ranges from 1 to 87,393 across 40,325 users. The built-in 'Community' account has user identifier -1 and reputation 1. Highest reputation denotes the most influential user.
scope: Comparing or ranking users by reputation

description: Vote creation dates are stored at day granularity without a time component, whereas comment, post and revision dates carry full timestamps. Comparisons requiring an exact time cannot be made on votes.
Recorded display names on comment rows are blank for 171,454 of 174,285 rows. The account's current display name in the user table is the reliable source; the recorded name is a fallback only.
scope: Resolving an author name from an action row

description: Timestamps are stored as text of the form '2013-07-12 09:08:18.0' with a space between the date and the time and a trailing '.0'. Question wording may present the same instant as '9:08:18 on 2013/7/12' or '2014/4/23 20:29:39'; a literal slash-formatted string does not match the stored value. Vote dates omit the time part entirely.
scope: Comparing a quoted date-time with stored timestamps

description: 1,392 posts have no owner user identifier. 1,388 of them carry a recorded owner display name instead (often a legacy label such as 'user28'), and 1,121 posts carry a recorded name alongside an owner identifier. The recorded name is a fallback for attribution when the identifier is absent, not a separate user key.
